newsitem.title: GERMANY: German CDU easily re-elects Kohl as party chairman.
newsitem.headline: German CDU easily re-elects Kohl as party chairman.

text.p: Germany's ruling Christian Democrats (CDU) re-elected Chancellor Helmut Kohl as their chairman on Monday for the 13th time with 95.5 percent support.
Kohl, 66, has headed the party for the past 23 years, 14 of them as chancellor, and was unopposed in the vote.
The chancellor told the CDU's annual congress earlier on Monday that he hoped his centre-right coalition with the liberal Free Democrats (FDP) would be re-elected for another four-year term in 1998.
Although he is widely expected to run again, he did not say whether he would be a candidate. After the vote, he raised his clasped hands like a victorious boxer and thanked the congress.
"Now let's get to work together," he said.
Kohl's re-election was so widely expected that there was no discussion before the 1,000 delegates cast their ballots.
While waiting for the votes to be counted, the chancellor sat and autographed copies of "I Wanted Gemany's Unity," a new book about his role in reunifying the two Germanys in 1990.
